scene-u01-pnew1-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew1-25.text: Training is not meant to memorise the points at hand

scene-u01-pnew1-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew1-26.text: The real goal is to predict unseen data well; this ability is called generalization.

scene-u01-pnew1-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew1-50.text:
unseen new data
(what we really predict)

scene-u01-pnew1-53.name: text#53
scene-u01-pnew1-53.text: KP04 showed: the tighter the fit to the training points, the further the training error sits below the new-data error. Now its consequences.

scene-u01-pnew1-55.name: text#55
scene-u01-pnew1-55.text: Training is for generalization, not for memorising the points at hand.

scene-u01-pnew2-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew2-25.text: By complexity, a model falls in one of three states

scene-u01-pnew2-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew2-26.text: Further right means a more complex model.

scene-u01-pnew2-33.name: text#33
scene-u01-pnew2-33.text: too simple: cannot even explain the training data

scene-u01-pnew2-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew2-43.text: too complex: memorises the training data and its noise, then does worse on new data

scene-u01-pnew2-74.name: text#74
scene-u01-pnew2-74.text: More complex is better? Not necessarily!

scene-u01-pnew2-76.name: text#76
scene-u01-pnew2-76.text: Too simple learns too little; too complex learns too much.

scene-u01-pnew3-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew3-25.text: The same 12 training points fitted with degree 1, 2 and 9

scene-u01-pnew3-94.name: text#94
scene-u01-pnew3-94.text: The line cannot bend; degree 2 hugs the truth; degree 9 hits every point yet swings wildly between them.

scene-u01-pnew4-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew4-25.text: Read the two errors: training MSE and test MSE

scene-u01-pnew4-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew4-26.text: MSE = mean squared error; the noise floor is $\sigma^2=0.09$ (KP03).

scene-u01-pnew4-35.name: text#35
scene-u01-pnew4-35.text: both high and almost equal: the mark of underfitting

scene-u01-pnew4-44.name: text#44
scene-u01-pnew4-44.text: both near the floor $0.09$: a good fit

scene-u01-pnew4-53.name: text#53
scene-u01-pnew4-53.text: training only $0.009$, an order below the floor, yet test $0.289$: overfitting

scene-u01-pnew4-55.name: text#55
scene-u01-pnew4-55.text: Training error far below test error (and below the noise floor) is the overfitting warning.

scene-u01-pnew5-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew5-25.text: The higher the degree, the more the training error falls

scene-u01-pnew5-72.name: text#72
scene-u01-pnew5-72.text: A higher degree contains the lower ones (set coefficients to $0$), so the least-squares training error cannot grow.

scene-u01-pnew5-94.name: text#94
scene-u01-pnew5-94.text: Training error falls monotonically with degree, down to just $0.0091$ at $d=9$.

scene-u01-pnew6-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew6-25.text: Test error falls then rises, lowest at $d=2$

scene-u01-pnew6-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew6-26.text: Units are MSE (computed), log vertical axis.

scene-u01-pnew6-84.name: text#84
scene-u01-pnew6-84.text:
$d=9$: $0.289$, already as bad as the line ($0.294$).
$d=10$: $0.440$ ≈ $4.9\times$ the floor.

scene-u01-pnew6-111.name: text#111
scene-u01-pnew6-111.text: Test error falls then rises: past some point, more complexity hurts on new data.

scene-u01-pnew7-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew7-25.text: The gap shows how little training error says about test error

scene-u01-pnew7-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew7-26.text: From $d=2$ onward the gap keeps widening.

scene-u01-pnew7-48.name: text#48
scene-u01-pnew7-48.text: ■ training MSE   ■ test MSE (bar heights to scale, reduced)

scene-u01-pnew7-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew7-50.text: Training error can fall below the floor: $d=9$'s $0.0091$ is about a tenth of $\sigma^2$, so the model memorised the noise.

scene-u01-pnew7-52.name: text#52
scene-u01-pnew7-52.text: Test error always sits above the floor (KP03): the best, $0.0963$, is only $0.0063$ above it.

scene-u01-pnew7-54.name: text#54
scene-u01-pnew7-54.text: Training error can drop below the noise floor, test error cannot: the plainest overfitting alarm.

scene-u01-pnew8-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew8-25.text: This is the result of one training set, not a law

scene-u01-pnew8-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew8-26.text: Another noise draw shifts the numbers slightly; the trend stays.

scene-u01-pnew8-73.name: text#73
scene-u01-pnew8-73.text: A new noise draw moves the numbers a little.

scene-u01-pnew8-75.name: text#75
scene-u01-pnew8-75.text: The trend stays: training falls throughout, test falls then rises.

scene-u01-pnew8-77.name: text#77
scene-u01-pnew8-77.text: Read the trend, not the last decimal.

scene-u01-pnew9-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew9-25.text: Why are degrees too low and too high both bad? Split the error in three

scene-u01-pnew9-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew9-26.text: Combining KP02 (bias and variance) with KP03 and KP04 (the noise floor).

scene-u01-pnew9-31.name: text#31
scene-u01-pnew9-31.text: how far the average fitted curve is from the truth (not accurate)

scene-u01-pnew9-34.name: text#34
scene-u01-pnew9-34.text: how much the curve moves with the training data (not stable)

scene-u01-pnew9-39.name: text#39
scene-u01-pnew9-39.text: The expectation is over re-drawn training sets: same 12 values of $x$, fresh noise each time, 2000 fits give 2000 curves.

scene-u01-pnew9-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew9-41.text: Error on new data = not accurate + not stable + noise floor.

scene-u01-pnew10-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew10-25.text: $d=1$: wrong in the same place every time (high bias, low variance)

scene-u01-pnew10-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew10-26.text: A line cannot bend, whichever training set is used.

scene-u01-pnew10-34.name: text#34
scene-u01-pnew10-34.text: $\mathrm{bias}^2=0.2084$, about two thirds of the total

scene-u01-pnew10-36.name: text#36
scene-u01-pnew10-36.text: $\mathrm{var}=0.0134$, tiny: any data gives about the same line

scene-u01-pnew10-40.name: text#40
scene-u01-pnew10-40.text: High bias, low variance = underfitting: bias dominates.

scene-u01-pnew11-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew11-25.text: $d=9$: a new noise draw changes the curve (low bias, high variance)

scene-u01-pnew11-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew11-26.text: The degree-9 polynomial contains the truth so it is right on average, but very unstable.

scene-u01-pnew11-48.name: text#48
scene-u01-pnew11-48.text: red = degree-9 fits on 8 different noise draws (illustration); dashed = the truth

scene-u01-pnew11-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew11-50.text: Low bias, high variance = overfitting: variance dominates.

scene-u01-pnew12-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew12-25.text: $d=2$ and $d=3$: both have bias $0$; only the variance differs

scene-u01-pnew12-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew12-26.text: Once the truth is contained, extra flexibility only adds variance.

scene-u01-pnew12-49.name: text#49
scene-u01-pnew12-49.text: As the degree rises, bias falls and variance rises: the bias–variance trade-off; neither can be minimised alone.

scene-u01-pnew12-51.name: text#51
scene-u01-pnew12-51.text: The $0.2066$ here averages over all possible training sets, hence it differs from the single-set $0.289$.

scene-u01-pnew12-53.name: text#53
scene-u01-pnew12-53.text: Bias and variance trade off: pick a degree in the middle.

scene-u01-pnew13-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew13-25.text: Choosing by training error always picks the most complex model

scene-u01-pnew13-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew13-26.text: Training error only falls as the degree rises.

scene-u01-pnew13-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew13-41.text: Its training error $0.0720$ is actually above $d=9$'s $0.0091$.

scene-u01-pnew13-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew13-43.text: What we want is low validation or test error; its training error may be higher.

scene-u01-pnew13-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew13-45.text: The model with the lowest training error is often not the best one.

scene-u01-pnew14-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew14-25.text: Read two numbers together to know whether to add or remove complexity

scene-u01-pnew14-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew14-26.text: The training error, and its gap to the validation error.

scene-u01-pnew14-34.name: text#34
scene-u01-pnew14-34.text: training error low, validation error much higher

scene-u01-pnew14-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew14-45.text: Complex models can also underfit: too little training, or too much regularisation.

scene-u01-pnew14-47.name: text#47
scene-u01-pnew14-47.text: "A big enough model never underfits" is not true.

scene-u01-pnew15-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew15-25.text: When two are about equally good, pick the simpler one; and we only have 12 points

scene-u01-pnew15-27.name: text#27
scene-u01-pnew15-27.text: A gap of only $0.0008$, far below the random wobble of one data set.

scene-u01-pnew15-36.name: text#36
scene-u01-pnew15-36.text: About equal error: pick the simpler model with fewer parameters and lower variance (added). KP07 turns this into a computable rule.

scene-u01-pnew15-39.name: text#39
scene-u01-pnew15-39.text: Choosing the degree needs data that did not train the model; using the test set is KP01's cheating #2.

scene-u01-pnew15-77.name: text#77
scene-u01-pnew15-77.text: With so little data, how to choose honestly and waste nothing? KP06 answers.

steps.label: KP05 · 1/15
steps.speakerNotes: Training is not for memorising the points at hand but for predicting unseen data well.

steps.speakerNotes: Training is not for memorising the points at hand but for predicting unseen data well.

steps.label: KP05 · 1/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: This ability is called generalization.

steps.label: KP05 · 1/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: KP04 showed that the tighter the fit, the lower the training error sits below the new-data error; this unit looks at the consequences.

steps.label: KP05 · 2/15
steps.speakerNotes: By complexity a model falls in one of three states.

steps.speakerNotes: By complexity a model falls in one of three states.

steps.label: KP05 · 2/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Underfit: too simple, cannot even explain the training data; good fit lies in between.

steps.label: KP05 · 2/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Overfit: too complex, memorises the training data and its noise, then does worse on new data.

steps.label: KP05 · 3/15
steps.speakerNotes: The same 12 training points (orange, fixed seed 11); the dashed line is the true function.

steps.speakerNotes: The same 12 training points (orange, fixed seed 11); the dashed line is the true function.

steps.label: KP05 · 3/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Degree 1 is a straight line that cannot bend; degree 2 hugs the truth.

steps.label: KP05 · 3/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Degree 9 passes through nearly every training point but swings wildly between them.

steps.label: KP05 · 4/15
steps.speakerNotes: Degree 1: training 0.288, test 0.294, both high and almost equal: underfitting.

steps.label: KP05 · 4/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Degree 1: training 0.288, test 0.294, both high and almost equal: underfitting.

steps.label: KP05 · 4/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Degree 2: training 0.072, test 0.096, both near the 0.09 floor.

steps.label: KP05 · 4/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Degree 9: training only 0.009, an order below the floor, but test 0.289.

steps.label: KP05 · 5/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The gold dashed line is the noise floor σ² = 0.09.

steps.label: KP05 · 5/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Training MSE falls monotonically: a higher degree contains the lower ones, so least squares cannot find a larger training error (added).

steps.label: KP05 · 6/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Lowest at d = 2, 0.0963, just above the floor.

steps.label: KP05 · 6/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: At d = 9 it is 0.289, already as bad as the line; at d = 10 0.440, about 4.9 times the floor.

steps.label: KP05 · 7/15
steps.speakerNotes: From d = 2 onward the orange training error keeps falling while the purple test error rises, and the gap widens.

steps.label: KP05 · 7/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: From d = 2 onward the orange training error keeps falling while the purple test error rises, and the gap widens.

steps.label: KP05 · 7/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The gap is how little training error says about test error.

steps.label: KP05 · 7/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Training MSE can fall below the floor: d = 9's 0.0091 is about a tenth of σ²; test MSE always stays above it, the best 0.0963 only 0.0063 higher. (Bars are scaled down.)

steps.label: KP05 · 8/15
steps.speakerNotes: The table is the result of one training set, so the numbers fluctuate a little.

steps.label: KP05 · 8/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The table is the result of one training set, so the numbers fluctuate a little.

steps.label: KP05 · 8/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: A new noise draw moves them slightly.

steps.label: KP05 · 8/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: But the trend does not: training error keeps falling, test error falls then rises.

steps.label: KP05 · 9/15
steps.speakerNotes: KP02 gave MSE = Var + Bias²; KP03 and KP04 add the unavoidable σ² for new data; at a fixed x they combine.

steps.label: KP05 · 9/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: KP02 gave MSE = Var + Bias²; KP03 and KP04 add the unavoidable σ² for new data; at a fixed x they combine.

steps.label: KP05 · 9/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: bias² is how far the average curve is from the truth, var how much the curve moves, σ² the noise floor.

steps.label: KP05 · 9/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The expectation is over re-drawn training sets: same 12 x values, fresh noise, 2000 fits give 2000 curves; then average over x.

steps.label: KP05 · 10/15
steps.speakerNotes: The line's bias² is 0.2084, two thirds of the total; its variance is only 0.0134.

steps.label: KP05 · 10/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The line's bias² is 0.2084, two thirds of the total; its variance is only 0.0134.

steps.label: KP05 · 10/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Whichever training set is used, it is wrong in the same place: high bias, low variance, i.e. underfitting.

steps.label: KP05 · 10/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Total 0.2084 + 0.0134 + 0.09 = 0.3118. (Lecture values; a seeded re-simulation agrees within 0.002.)

steps.label: KP05 · 11/15
steps.speakerNotes: Fitting degree 9 on 8 different noise draws (illustration) gives wildly different curves.

steps.label: KP05 · 11/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Fitting degree 9 on 8 different noise draws (illustration) gives wildly different curves.

steps.label: KP05 · 11/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: It contains the truth so bias² ≈ 0, but the variance is 0.1166, about 6 times that of d = 2.

steps.label: KP05 · 11/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Total 0 + 0.1166 + 0.09 = 0.2066: low bias, high variance, i.e. overfitting.

steps.label: KP05 · 12/15
steps.speakerNotes: d = 2 and d = 3 both have bias 0 since both contain the quadratic truth; the table's 0.0000 is zero within simulation error.

steps.label: KP05 · 12/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: d = 2 and d = 3 both have bias 0 since both contain the quadratic truth; the table's 0.0000 is zero within simulation error.

steps.label: KP05 · 12/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Only the variance differs: d = 3 has one more parameter, variance rises from 0.019 to 0.025.

steps.label: KP05 · 12/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: As the degree grows bias falls and variance rises, the bias–variance trade-off. The earlier 0.289 is this one data set; 0.207 here averages over all possible training sets.

steps.label: KP05 · 13/15
steps.speakerNotes: Choosing by training error always picks the most complex model: here d = 10, with test MSE 0.440, among the worst.

steps.label: KP05 · 13/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Choosing by training error always picks the most complex model: here d = 10, with test MSE 0.440, among the worst.

steps.label: KP05 · 13/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: We should choose low validation or test error: d = 2, whose training MSE 0.0720 is above d = 9's 0.0091.

steps.label: KP05 · 13/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The lowest training error is often not the best model.

steps.label: KP05 · 14/15
steps.speakerNotes: Both high and close: underfitting, add complexity.

steps.label: KP05 · 14/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Both high and close: underfitting, add complexity.

steps.label: KP05 · 14/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Training low but validation much higher: overfitting, reduce complexity or suppress it with the regularisation of KP07 onward.

steps.label: KP05 · 14/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Both near the noise floor: a good fit. Complex models can still underfit through too little training or too much regularisation.

steps.label: KP05 · 15/15
steps.speakerNotes: d = 2 and d = 3 have test MSE 0.0963 and 0.0971, a gap of 0.0008, far below one data set's random wobble.

steps.label: KP05 · 15/15 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: d = 2 and d = 3 have test MSE 0.0963 and 0.0971, a gap of 0.0008, far below one data set's random wobble.

steps.label: KP05 · 15/15 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Pick the simpler one: about equal error with fewer parameters and lower variance (added); KP07 turns this into a computable rule.

steps.label: KP05 · 15/15 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Choosing the degree needs data that did not train the model; using the test set is KP01's cheating #2, so a validation set is needed. With only 12 points, what now? KP06's cross-validation.
